稼.meaning: A mouse runs a tiny bakery in a doll's <part>house</part>, buying one <part>grain</part> at a time from the barn and baking it into loaves for the beetles. By winter, the doll's house is stuffed with buttons and coins. Not bad <kanji>earnings</kanji> for a mouse.
稼.on: She banks the lot with a fat orange <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond.
稼.kun: Every evening she counts it into a <sound>cu</sound>p, <sound>se</sound>ven coins at a time.

浪.meaning: A <part>good</part> little robot is told to go and see the world. It follows the <part>water drops</part> from a dripping tap down the drain, into the river and out to the open sea, waving at every fish. It never picks a home: it is happiest <kanji>wandering</kanji>.
浪.on: Someone on a bridge tosses it a red <sound>ro</sound>se as it drifts by.

錯.meaning: A treasure hunter digs up <part>gold</part> coins from <part>antiquity</part>, each from a different empire, and tries to pay for a coffee with them. The cashier stares, the till beeps, and the coffee machine spits out soup. Everyone in the café is <kanji>confused</kanji>.
錯.on: In the end she swaps one coin for a fat <sound>suc</sound>culent by the till.

枯.meaning: In an office, everyone forgets to water the <part>old</part> potted <part>tree</part> in the corner, but they keep hanging their coats on it. One Monday it droops, drops its last leaves on the boss's desk and sighs. Without water, even an office plant will <kanji>wither</kanji>.
枯.on: A stuffed toy <sound>ko</sound>ala clings to its last bare branch.
枯.kun: At last someone tips in the water from the <sound>car</sound>p bowl.

斜.meaning: A greedy cook scoops <part>too much</part> soup into her <part>ladle</part>, and the weight tips it over at a steep angle. Soup runs down the handle and across her white apron in one stripe from corner to corner. Every apron in that kitchen has the same <kanji>diagonal</kanji> stain.
斜.on: She tries to bat the drips away with a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock.
斜.kun: Then she mops up the rest with <sound>na</sound>an and <sound>na</sound>chos.

撤.meaning: Packing day at the circus: the strongman hooks an <part>anchor</part> into the big top and drags it down, the crew <part>bring up</part> the tent pegs one by one, and the ringmaster waves a giant <part>fan</part> to blow the sawdust away. By sunset the field is empty grass. They <kanji>remove</kanji> a whole circus in a day.
撤.on: All that's left behind is a bowl with one tiny <sound>tet</sound>ra fish.
